Within the randomized nivo/chemo arm (Arm A1), baseline circulating T-cell populations that looked most favorable as associative biomarkers of 1-year overall survival were higher NKT cells, higher Tbet+ T cells, and higher Tbet+ TCRgd+ T cells. In the 25 A1 patients with baseline CyTOF, median-split Kaplan-Meier analysis gave: NKT cells (% leukocytes), 1-year KM survival 0.900 in the high group vs 0.364 in the low group (log-rank p=0.00494, BH q=0.0247); Tbet+ T cells (% CD3), 0.808 vs 0.455 (p=0.0106, q=0.0247); and Tbet+ TCRgd+ T cells (% TCRgd), 0.808 vs 0.455 (p=0.0250, q=0.0437). The strongest adverse baseline association was higher Ki-67+ T cells (% CD3), with 1-year KM survival 0.333 in the high group vs 1.000 in the low group (p=0.00998, q=0.0247). HLA-DR+ total T cells, HLA-DR+ non-naive CD4 T cells, and HLA-DR+ non-naive CD8 T cells were not significantly associated with OS in this subset.

Interpretation: in this dataset, a baseline peripheral immune profile enriched for NKT-like / T-bet-positive effector-like T-cell features was associated with better 1-year survival under nivo/chemo, whereas a higher fraction of proliferating Ki-67+ T cells was associated with worse survival. However, this is an associative, not causal, analysis. The analyzable subset was small (25 profiled patients), and 9 of 34 A1 patients had no baseline CyTOF sample; all 9 of those unprofiled patients died, so selection bias is a major limitation. These findings should therefore be treated as exploratory baseline biomarkers within the profiled subset, not as definitive predictive markers for nivolumab benefit.
